clue.text: One gathering material from street and river to use in artwork

indicators.note: the two abbreviations are put to use inside the word for the artwork, splitting it

parts.note: a drawing is a piece of artwork
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone collects scraps from the street and the river for an art project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to use in' signals a container. 'One gathering material' reads like a scavenger, but it is the cord that gathers cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord threaded through a hem pulls fabric into gathers, so it is something that gathers material.

clue.text: Lose a lot of faith with many heartless around

indicators.note: the shortened many is placed around the shortened faith
without its heart, the word many loses its two middle letters

parts.note: taken as written before being cut

indicators.note: most of the word for the faith is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: Islam is a religious faith

explanation.surface: Someone fears losing much of their faith when surrounded by many who lack heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle AN; 'a lot of' drops the faith's last letter; 'around' wraps one shortened word round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to lose it by putting it somewhere and forgetting where.

clue.text: Odd pun comic broadcast

indicators.note: comic suggests the letters of pun are played about with into a new order

parts.note: something broadcast has been aired

explanation.surface: A strange joke goes out on air in a comedy show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' rearranges PUN to UNP, followed by AIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd sock is one without its partner, i.e. unpaired.

clue.text: Bird used wings, heading off after dog

indicators.note: the second piece follows the dog in the answer

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is taken off the word for used wings

parts.note: a bird that used its wings flew

explanation.surface: A bird flapped off ahead after being chased by a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the first letter of the past tense for using wings; 'after' places that remainder behind the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The curlew is a long-billed wading bird of moors and estuaries.

clue.text: Advocate drive over Portugal for scenery

parts.note: to advocate a cause is to back it
DR is the abbreviation for drive in addresses
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Someone urges a road trip through Portugal to see the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted backdrop is the scenery hung at the back of a stage.

clue.text: Uncovered some bits in skip

indicators.note: with their outer letters stripped away, each word shows only its inside

explanation.surface: Parts of a dumped load of rubbish lie exposed in a skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' leaves OM from SOME and IT from BITS. A skip in Britain is a large open bin for builders' rubbish, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip a passage or item is to leave it out.

clue.text: Transport returning home carrying advanced alien

indicators.note: returning means the word for the transport is read backwards

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport

indicators.note: the word for home holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A tram heads back to the depot with an extraterrestrial on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TRAM into MART; 'carrying' puts A in IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A being from Mars is the classic fictional extraterrestrial.

clue.text: One getting on in education

parts.note: getting on suggests progressing in one's studies, but means growing older: an adult learner

explanation.surface: Someone is doing well at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who starts college or university past the usual age is an older learner, i.e. one getting on in years.

clue.text: Defenceless Cockney's not hurt

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H sound from the start of words

parts.note: someone not hurt is unharmed

explanation.surface: A London East Ender gets through a scrape without a scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops initial H; 'Cockney's' removes the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone carrying no weapons is without defence.

clue.text: Game residents played to create quarrels

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of the two words are performed in a different order

explanation.surface: Locals play a match that ends up causing rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges GAME RESIDENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarrels are arguments, rows or fallings-out between people.

clue.text: Wall I tore out to make place for drier

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of order and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A wall was torn down to make room for a clothes drier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WALL I TORE. The drier is not a machine but the cloth you dry yourself with.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar on which bath sheets hang is where the thing that dries you is kept.

clue.text: Birds strip outer covering of eucalyptus

parts.note: a football strip is a team's kit

indicators.note: the outer covering of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Birds peel the bark from a eucalyptus tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outer covering of' takes the first and last letters of the tree. Strip is a noun here, a sports team's outfit, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Kites are birds of prey with forked tails.

clue.text: Another shot tyre repaired on right

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the rearranged tyre comes after right
repaired suggests the letters of tyre are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A mechanic has another go at a tyre that was mended on the right-hand wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges the tyre's letters; 'on' sets them after the abbreviation for right.
explanation.definitionFit: To have another try at something is to take another shot at it.

clue.text: Editing on and on …

parts.note: RE means on, as in on the subject of
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone keeps editing a text, going on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses of 'on' give the two halves; the ellipsis runs the clue into 15 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Reworking a text means revising it, which is what editing does.

clue.text: Some nomadic eland, erstwhile natives of volcanic land

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some wandering antelope were once at home in a land of volcanoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a volcanic island, so its people are natives of a volcanic land.

clue.text: … after move, editor is put off

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the editor follows the word for move

parts.note: to shift is to move

explanation.surface: Continuing 13 Across: after being moved around, the editor gets fed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like 'disgusted', but means postponed.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting that is postponed has been moved to a later time.

clue.text: Individual northbound in confines of trimaran noticed cutter

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the outer letters of trimaran
the confines of a word are its boundary letters, first and last
in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: one means a single individual
to have noticed something is to have saw it, past tense of see

explanation.surface: A single person heading north inside a trimaran spotted a cutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northbound' reverses the individual; 'confines of' takes the boat's end letters; 'in' puts the first inside the second. The cutter looks like a sailing vessel but is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small stiff-backed saw for fine joinery cuts.

clue.text: Consume tons in peeled bananas

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
bananas means crazy, so the letters of peeled go wild

explanation.surface: Someone eats loads of peeled bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges PEELED to DEPLEE; 'in' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a stock is to use it up, i.e. consume it.

clue.text: Deputation from Washington catching eagle freaking out Yankee

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the capital holds the rearranged bird inside it

parts.note: DC, District of Columbia, is how Washington is written

indicators.note: a bird freaking out is in a frenzy, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A delegation from Washington nets a panicking eagle before an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freaking out' rearranges the bird; 'catching' puts it inside the capital's abbreviation, and Yankee's letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegacy is a body of delegates, i.e. a deputation sent to act for others.

clue.text: Coarse man apprehended by a French revolutionary general

indicators.note: the word for man is caught and held between the other pieces

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: revolutionary means the general's name is turned round

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A rough fellow is arrested by a revolutionary French general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the Civil War general round into a fish; 'apprehended by' holds the man between the French article and that fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungenteel means lacking refinement or polite manners, i.e. vulgar.

clue.text: Spain provided iron and lead for local engineer

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain
if means provided, as in on condition that
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Spain supplied iron and lead to a local engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead for' takes L from LOCAL. The lead looks like the metal, matching iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Eiffel was the French engineer behind the Paris tower bearing his name.

clue.text: Gorge cold meat, eating starter in steakhouse

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

indicators.note: the meat takes the letter inside it

parts.note: ham is a kind of meat

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs down cold meat while eating a first course at a steakhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter in' gives S from STEAKHOUSE; 'eating' puts it inside HAM. 'Gorge' looks like a verb about eating, but is a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm is a deep cleft in the ground, like a ravine.

clue.text: Concerned about a clique

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a ring is a closed group, like a clique or gang

explanation.surface: Someone worries about an exclusive set of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone caring shows concern for other people.

clue.text: Dainty foxtrot involved in line dancing

indicators.note: the letter becomes part of the rearranged word, inside it
dancing suggests the letters of line move about

parts.note: Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A delicate dancer takes part in a foxtrot during a line dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges LINE to ELIN; 'involved in' puts F inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes something small and delicate, like a fairy.

clue.text: Fine swimmer's instinct

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an eel is a swimmer; the 's stands for is, linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A good swimmer has a natural instinct for the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A feel for something is an instinctive knack or aptitude.

clue.text: Expected form tutor

parts.note: a figure is a shape or form
a don is a university tutor at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's class teacher was anticipated.
explanation.walkthrough: A form tutor is the teacher in charge of a British school class, but 'form' and 'tutor' split apart here.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure on something is to count on it, i.e. expect it.

clue.text: Adolescent's eaten crackers by case in glee

indicators.note: crackers means mad, so the letters of eaten go wild
the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: A youngster has gleefully devoured some biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' rearranges EATEN to TEENA; 'case in' gives GE from GLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage describes someone aged thirteen to nineteen, that is youthful and adolescent.

clue.text: Money from abroad secures soldiers meeting places

indicators.note: the money holds the soldiers fast inside it

parts.note: cents are coins used in many foreign currencies
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps

explanation.surface: Foreign cash secures troops where people gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' holds the soldiers inside the coins. Royal Engineers is a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Centres such as community centres are hubs where people gather.
